title: Saint
description: One saint as one entity with N per-church attestations. There is no merged row and no single truth: a figure venerated by one church and refused by another carries both, side by side, unresolved.

slug.description: Permanent id. Must equal the folder name.

display_name.$comment: The bare name, and only the name (author, 2026-08-27). It used to hold name, office, rank and death year in one string - "Gorazd, Bishop of Bohemia and Moravia-Silesia, Hieromartyr (1942)" - which is why the site could only ever prefix "St.": any other honorific would have collided with a rank already sitting in the string. The rank is read from `types`, the office is the field below, and the year is in `dates.death`; none of the three belongs here.

office.$comment: What the figure held, not what they are called: "Presbyter", "Bishop of Sardis", "Metropolitan of Moschonisia". Printed on the subtext line beside the dates, never in the name - the rank is short and is how a saint is named, the office is long and is a fact about them, so the long half goes on the line that can truncate without losing the identity.

kind.$comment: A folder is a saint unless it says otherwise. The one alternative is a feast: when the Great Feasts become folders, "St. Dormition of the Theotokos" is what a blanket honorific would print, so the naming function opts out on this flag rather than on a guess about the name (saints-naming-addendum.md, Step 3). Nothing in the corpus carries it yet; it is here before the work that needs it, not after.

track.description: An ordered journey with years on it: where the sources place this person, and from when until when. Separate from `locations`, which is an unordered set of kinds carrying no dates at all — a bishop's see and a saint's relics are facts about a life, not moments in it. The map reads this to move the dot as the timeline crosses the life; without it a saint has one dot chosen by year, which is all the corpus can honestly say about almost everyone.

hymns.$comment: The troparion and kontakion a church sings for the figure, in that church's own language, copied whole from the cited source with the tone it prints (author, 2026-08-22). A hymn belongs to a church, as an attestation does: the Greek apolytikion and the Romanian tropar are different texts, not translations of one.

model.$comment: The automelon the hymn is sung to, where the source names it.

english.$comment: A published English rendering of this same hymn, where one exists in a source this site may copy (author, 2026-08-26). Not a translation made here — Amendment 2 forbids that — and not a different church's hymn: the same text, rendered, with its own citation. Isabel Hapgood's 1906 Service Book is the one source used so far, being long in the public domain; a modern translation is a living author's work and needs their permission, which is the author's decision and not a build's.

interval.description: Every date is an interval. A precise date has equal bounds. A null bound is an open bound — a real finding, such as 'no later than 550' — and is not the same as an absent date.

oneOf.description: Movable feast, as a signed day offset from Pascha. The computus is taken from the church unless stated here.

rank.$comment: The typikon's rank of the service this church keeps for the figure, where the source states it — vigil, polyeleos, great doxology, six stichera, or a simple service. It is what the red-letter idiom is for in this tradition, and it is a sourced editorial datum, not an inference from a date.

allOf.$comment: A veneration and a refusal are both positive findings and both need a citation. Only 'undocumented' — we have not looked, or looked and found nothing — may stand without one, which is exactly what makes it different from a refusal.
A feast day is a claim about veneration and cannot be attached to a refusal or a gap.

uncertainty_km.description: Radius of uncertainty in kilometres — a number, not an enum, so halos, cluster thresholds and label logic are one continuous function of one field (Addendum B1). Authoring defaults: pinpointed site 1, city 15, region 150, 'somewhere in this province' 500. Required whenever coordinates are present.

waypoint.description: One stay on a `track`. `from` and `to` are the years the sources place the person here; a null `from` on the first stay means 'from birth, the year unrecorded' and a null `to` on the last means 'until death'. Between one stay's `to` and the next's `from` the map draws the dot moving, which is the one thing on a track that is drawn rather than sourced — where someone travelled between two attested places is almost never recorded, and the `note` on each stay is where that is said in words.
